question: What primary shift characterizes the epidemiological transition currently occurring in Nigeria?

options.A: A rapid decrease in overall population growth rates
options.B: A shift from urban to rural disease distribution
options.C: The complete eradication of vector-borne illnesses
options.D: The simultaneous burden of infectious and chronic diseases

explanation: Nigeria and many developing nations are experiencing a dual disease burden, managing both traditional infectious diseases and rising rates of non-communicable chronic conditions. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T1#GNS313_U3_T1_h1)

question: Which of the following is considered a non-modifiable risk factor for non-communicable diseases?
explanation: Age, genetic makeup, and family history are intrinsic biological factors that cannot be altered, unlike behavioral habits such as diet and exercise. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T1#GNS313_U3_T1_h2)

question: How do modifiable risk factors primarily influence the development of chronic conditions?

options.A: They interact with biological vulnerabilities to accelerate cellular and vascular damage
options.B: They exclusively affect the lymphatic system within the first decade of life
options.C: They directly alter an individual's inherited genetic code over time
options.D: They prevent the body from absorbing essential micronutrients permanently

explanation: Lifestyle habits and environmental exposures compound over time, straining organ systems and promoting the pathological changes that manifest as chronic illnesses. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T1#GNS313_U3_T1_h2)

question: What is the primary objective of primary prevention strategies in healthcare?

options.A: To diagnose asymptomatic pathology using advanced laboratory tests
options.B: To rehabilitate patients following a major surgical intervention
options.C: To prevent the initial onset of disease in a healthy population
options.D: To halt the progression of an established clinical disease

explanation: Primary prevention focuses on risk reduction and health promotion before any pathological changes or disease states occur. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T1#GNS313_U3_T1_h3)

question: A community health nurse in a Nigerian market square wants to promote healthy nutrition. What is the most practical approach?

options.A: Promoting balanced meals using affordable, locally available foodstuffs
options.B: Instructing community members to fast for two days every week
options.C: Advocating for the exclusive consumption of raw, unprocessed grains
options.D: Distributing meal plans based exclusively on imported dietary supplements

explanation: Effective health promotion must be culturally appropriate and economically feasible, leveraging local agricultural produce that community members can easily access and afford. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T1#GNS313_U3_T1_h3)

question: What defines secondary prevention in the continuum of healthcare?

options.A: Enacting national legislation to ban harmful industrial pollutants
options.B: Providing palliative comfort measures for terminal illnesses
options.C: Screening for early, asymptomatic disease to allow prompt treatment
options.D: Restoring physical mobility following a disabling stroke

explanation: Secondary prevention targets individuals with early or subclinical disease through screening tests to catch conditions before they cause severe damage. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T1#GNS313_U3_T1_h4)

question: What is the main advantage of implementing opportunistic screening in busy Nigerian primary healthcare clinics?

options.A: It guarantees 100 percent compliance with prescribed dietary regimens
options.B: It captures individuals who would otherwise not attend routine wellness visits
options.C: It completely replaces the necessity for long-term pharmacological treatment
options.D: It eliminates the need for any diagnostic equipment whatsoever

explanation: Since routine preventive health checks are uncommon, screening patients who present for acute ailments maximizes the opportunity to detect hidden chronic conditions. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T1#GNS313_U3_T1_h4)

question: Which factor represents a major barrier to chronic medication adherence in many Nigerian clinical settings?

options.A: Excessive availability of free pharmaceutical supplies
options.B: Overly simplistic dosing schedules prescribed by physicians
options.C: Too few chronic conditions existing within the population
options.D: Out-of-pocket costs and fake or substandard drugs

explanation: Financial constraints combined with the risk of purchasing counterfeit medications severely undermine consistent long-term drug therapy for chronic illnesses. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T1#GNS313_U3_T1_h5)

question: Why must the management of non-communicable diseases differ from acute care approaches?

options.A: Chronic diseases never require laboratory monitoring or diagnostic testing
options.B: Acute care is exclusively practiced in rural community health posts
options.C: Chronic diseases always resolve spontaneously without medical intervention
options.D: Acute care focuses on permanent cures, whereas chronic care requires lifelong management

explanation: Unlike a short-term infection that resolves with a course of antibiotics, chronic conditions persist indefinitely and require sustained lifestyle and pharmacological management. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T1#GNS313_U3_T1_h5)

question: What is a primary responsibility of the community health nurse in NCD control?

options.A: Manufacturing pharmaceutical drugs for national distribution
options.B: Performing complex open-heart surgeries in primary clinics
options.C: Conducting community outreach, screening, and health education
options.D: Enforcing strict punitive fines for unhealthy dietary habits

explanation: Community health nurses focus on health promotion, early detection through screening, and educating populations directly within their local environments. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T1#GNS313_U3_T1_h6)

question: Why is establishing patient support groups valuable for individuals managing chronic illnesses?

options.A: They replace the professional nursing assessment process entirely
options.B: They supply free imported medications to all participating members
options.C: They provide emotional encouragement and foster shared coping strategies
options.D: They completely eliminate the need for ongoing medical check-ups

explanation: Support groups build social capital and psychological resilience, helping patients navigate the challenges of living with a lifelong condition. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T1#GNS313_U3_T1_h6)

question: Which of the following interventions is an example of a fiscal policy used to control non-communicable diseases?

options.A: Mandating hospital admission for individuals with high cholesterol
options.B: Placing high taxes on sugar-sweetened beverages and tobacco
options.C: Banning the construction of all commercial food markets
options.D: Providing free gym memberships for every citizen over age sixty

explanation: Taxation policies make unhealthy products less affordable, effectively reducing consumption at the population level. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T1#GNS313_U3_T1_h7)

question: Why is multisectoral collaboration essential for effective non-communicable disease control?

options.A: International donors will not fund health programs managed by nurses
options.B: Medical doctors refuse to collaborate with nurses on chronic disease management
options.C: Infectious diseases can only be controlled by agricultural ministries
options.D: Health ministries alone cannot influence the underlying social and environmental determinants of health

explanation: The root causes of NCDs—such as diet, physical environment, and commercial product marketing—are governed by sectors outside of traditional healthcare, necessitating a whole-of-government approach. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T1#GNS313_U3_T1_h7)
